routes.reason: Accept as corrected. RF0's text is 'For a perfect F_q-algebra R construct W_OE(R), its Teichmüller representatives, Frobenius and the pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property ... Prove functoriality, reduction, topology and uniformizer-change comparisons.' Its packet node RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property builds W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect R. Nothing else in the atlas owns ramified Witt vectors: QWittVectors plans big Witt vectors only. So §1.2 (Witt polynomials, Dwork's criterion, F and V_π, change of E, the Q-twisted functor, the Lubin–Tate Teichmüller lifts) belongs here, and RF0's blueprint must state it for arbitrary π-adic O_E-algebras (PROTOCOL §15, most general form). The review added RF1 and item 94 (from the rejected FarguesFontaineDiamonds route): Remarque 3.19's diamond identity for general E is RF1's 'diamond formulas over Perf_Fq with the chosen coefficient-field embedding' ((Y_S)^◇ = S × Spd E), whereas F1 is for E = Q_p only. Item 114 now carries the corrected formula of E25.

Accept as corrected. Nothing in the atlas proves the function theory of the variable π on which the book builds the curve. That covers primitive elements and their factorisation into degree-one primitives (Théorème 2.4.1), zeros, divisors and the slope/zero correspondence (2.4.11, 3.4.4), principality of B_I (2.5.1, 3.5.1), Galois descent of points and of B (3.1.8, 3.3.1, 3.6.1), graded factoriality of P (6.2.1), the fundamental exact sequence for general points (6.4.1), and the schematic curve over a perfect F that is not algebraically closed, with B_{F,e} Dedekind and Cl(B_{F,e}) ≅ Hom(G_F, E^×) (7.2.1, 7.2.4, 7.3.3). RF0:annuli and RF3 construct the objects ('construct Y_S ... and the annulus rings'; 'Form the graded algebra ... construct Proj'). F4 says 'This stage does not assert a classification of all closed points for an arbitrary non-algebraically-closed F', and VB2:ampleness covers only 'S a geometric perfectoid point'. The routes pass proposed moving Théorème 3.5.7, Corollaire 3.5.8 and Lemme 11.2.6 to RD.0; I rejected that move. RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid, analytic-ring-bezout and vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free all assume 'v_ℓ discrete', and RD.0/extended-robba-ring treats only the completed algebraic closure of k((t)), so a general perfectoid F is not covered and the extraction's reason was right. Corrections: the brief now names every import by title and id, and adds the existing Tau Ceti Foundations of adic spaces Layer 6 (never re-planned) and P7:annulus-foundations. It records that RD.0 must import the non-discrete case from here. It restricts Théorème 6.2.7's surjectivity and Théorème 6.4.1 to F algebraically closed (pp. 247, 253), and gives 3.5.1's radius condition ρ ∉ |F|^{1/∞} for perfect F. The route gained Chapter 4.1 (405–415) from route 4, the 21 items whose planned status the review corrected (Kedlaya's rings over non-discrete or equal-characteristic coefficients, intervals containing 1, θ for general algebras, 2.3.13, 2.5.1(2), §3.4.1, §11.2 bundles on Y_I) and new items 1108–1109. It lost item 707 (now planned at VB2:ampleness). The brief must carry the review's corrections E198 (Théorème 2.5.1(2) and 3.5.1(2): the isomorphism is |Y_{I∖{0}}| ⥲ Spm(B_I)), E199 (Proposition 3.1.7) and E211 (Théorème 6.4.4 needs the orbit hypothesis of 6.4.1).

Accept as corrected. No layer owns the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5 (VB1 'Build[s] degree, rank, slope, saturated subbundles and semistability' for bundles on the curve only), the Riemann spheres and classification criteria of §5.6, the classification over a perfect F that is not algebraically closed and π_1 (VB0: 'A classification after algebraic closure is not a classification of all descent forms over an arbitrary perfectoid field'), the φ-module descriptions over B^+, B^+_ρ and B^+_cris,ρ, or Colmez's 𝒞 and Fontaine's almost C-representations. These continue VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, so a Part II is right. Corrections: (a) the route reused the id VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII of the accepted PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2 but with a different title. Id, parent and area already matched, so the title is now byte-identical to the accepted one, and the brief carries the extension. (b) Colmez's Dimension and the category BC (27, 28, 837, 838) went to the VB3 source route (route 8), because Colmez–Nizioł imports the Dimension formalism from the parent and its accepted route 3 routed it to VB0–VB3. (c) The review brought in the abstract HN formalism and O(d,h) on generalized Riemann spheres (590–603, 606, 608, 610, 619, 641, 647–652, 661). These were marked planned in VB1 or VB2 although those layers plan them only on the Fargues–Fontaine curve. It also brought in the φ-module items 1019 and 1100, FF's bundle dictionary (1085, 1086, 1099, from route 6) and Weinstein's π_1 computations (96, 97, from the rejected route 8), which are the diamond form of Théorèmes 8.6.1 and 9.5.1. (d) Théorème 9.2.2 assumes F algebraically closed (p. 306). The brief must carry E105, E106, E109, E114 and E153.

Accept as corrected. R07.2 'Construct[s] Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields ... Supply the deformation results needed for p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings' and stops there. No layer owns Fontaine's covectors, the periods G(O_F) ≅ Hom(D[1/π], B^+), the universal cover X(G) as a formal E-vector space, the images of the Gross–Hopkins and Drinfeld period maps (Théorèmes 8.1.1, 8.1.3), or Proposition 8.3.2. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a constructs the towers and period morphisms, but no image theorem. These are theorems about π-divisible modules, so FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory is the right parent, and its Part IIs fold into one design job. Corrections: the prismatic Dieudonné Part II (SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20 route 1) also plans the universal cover. The brief's 'compared rather than duplicated' left two owners, so it now says X(G) is built here for any ring with π nilpotent and imported there. ET.6a imports Théorèmes 8.1.1 and 8.1.3 from here, and VB3:positive-basic-examples' Lubin–Tate calculation is imported. All imports are named by title and id. Chapter 4.1 (405–415) moved to route 2. The route gained 452, 498, 510 and 774 (status corrections: the atlas plans them only in special cases).

Accept as corrected. R06.2 ('Prove weak admissibility versus admissibility') and R06.3 ('Prove the p-adic monodromy theorem') plan both end theorems for K/Q_p finite, by the Colmez–Fontaine and Berger routes. 'B-pair' appears in no stage or packet node, and nothing plans G_K-equivariant bundles, X_log, Théorème 10.1.7 or Berger's 11.5.1. The accepted PadicHodgeTheory Part IIs (generic monodromy, relative crystalline local systems) do not touch them. The review added the Chapter 10 items that the atlas plans only for K/Q_p finite, since Chapter 10 works over any complete discretely valued K with perfect residue field: Tate's theorems, B_cris regular, the Tate-curve remarks, Théorème 10.5.7 and Remarque 10.5.8, the monodromy theorem, inflation–restriction with Banach coefficients, Proposition 10.6.18(1) and Remarque 10.6.19 (882, 903, 923, 924, 934, 964, 966, 979, 995, 998, 1000). The Part II must therefore state the two main theorems in that generality and prove them agree with R06.2/R06.3 for K/Q_p finite. It also gained item 1103 from route 9, the decompletion of all (not only étale) (φ,Γ)-modules. Two links were added to the brief. B-pairs are owned and exported here, for TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel (PAPER-DING-25), which expects them from P7, a stage that does not plan them. And one owner must be named, with AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures, for 'filtrations versus B_dR^+-lattices'. The brief must carry E156, E159, E167, E168 and E215.

Accept as corrected. RD.0 'Build[s] bounded and full Robba rings with their radius-indexed norms and topology' and RD.1 the Frobenius slope filtrations. Its packet has Lazard (closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid), Bézout and closed ideals, and Kedlaya's descent statements. Lazard (59–61), the closed ideals of the Robba ring (64), Kedlaya's φ-Mod_{E^†} → φ-Mod_ℰ (1087), the lattice lemma (1089), coker(Id − π^{−d}φ^h) = 0 on E^† (1088) and Remarque 11.3.4 (1096) belong there. RD.0 and RD.1 must state them for E of equal characteristic too, since Kedlaya's Γ^ℓ is built over a Cohen ring. Items 1087 and 1089 are false as printed (E218, E219). Their items carry Kedlaya's correct statements (a slope filtration, not a decomposition; bijective φ), and the layers must not inherit the printed forms. Items 1085, 1086 and 1099 moved to route 3; 384, 385 and 1058 stay in route 2 (see route 2).

Accept. R06.1 plans Tate–Sen theory (packet nodes R06.1/tate-sen-theorem and semilinear-galois-descent), where Sen's theorem belongs (10, 983). R06.2 plans weak admissibility versus admissibility, and Colmez–Fontaine's neighbouring representations (18–22) are one of its proof routes. R06.3 carries Berger's proof (R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem defers to it), so Berger's ∆(D) and his monodromy theorem for non-étale (φ,Γ)-modules (83–86, 89) belong there. Proposition 2.9 uses Colmez's 𝒞 (route 3). R06.2 then imports from the VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals Part II, which is acyclic.

The extraction's route 8, a source route to FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1 and F3 (items 94, 96, 97), is rejected. F1 is 'α_F : Y_F^◇ ≅ S × Spd(Q_p)', for E = Q_p only. F3 is 'actual equivalences of sites and of finite étale categories', and computes no π_1. Item 94 went to route 1 (RF1) and items 96–97 to route 3. The slot now holds the source route to VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3 and VB3:general-BC ('For the positive-slope range prove dimension and cohomological smoothness'), with items 27, 28, 837 and 838. These are Colmez's Dimension (dim, ht), well defined and additive, and the abelian category BC. The accepted PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 3 routed the same statement (its Proposition 3.2) to VB0–VB3. I accept this route as it now stands.

Accept as corrected. PG.0 'Include[s] field-of-norms Galois equivalence and the descent/lifting statements required in Fontaine's construction'. The field of norms of the Kummer tower (391) is that theory for an arithmetically profinite tower other than the cyclotomic one, so PG.0's blueprint must state it for APF extensions. The decompletion of §11.5 (1103) concerns all (φ,Γ)-modules and moved to route 5. PG.2 ('the larger category of all Robba (φ,Γ)-modules') now takes the tilde-ring clauses of Préface Théorème 2.41(i) and (iii) (78, 80), which it plans only over B_rig,K.

notes: Accept, with the extraction corrected in place. The review read courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017, SHA-256 cc159f38…922ca3, matching the record). It was split into nine chapter passes and four status passes, with every sourceIssue and every formula that mattered checked on 300-dpi page images. Items: 44 statements, 4 locators and many notes were corrected, and 3 items added (1107 Préface Théorème 3.16, planned at RF0:annuli; 1108 Remarque 1.4.4; 1109 Exemples 2.3.7/2.3.10). Statuses: 65 planned items became missing, because the cited layer plans only a special case: K/Q_p finite for Chapter 10's K; E of characteristic 0 or discretely valued coefficients for Kedlaya's rings; the Fargues–Fontaine curve for the abstract HN and Riemann-sphere theory of Chapter 5; perfectoid rings for θ. One item became planned (707, VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence). The counts are now 1109 items: 15 library, 181 planned, 913 missing. Routes: all nine accepted as corrected. Route 3 joins the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII with its byte-identical title. The original route 8 (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1/F3) was rejected and its slot re-used for a VB3 source route. Items moved between routes as recorded in the report. A proposed move of Kedlaya's Bézout theorem to RD.0 was rejected, because RD.0's nodes assume v_ℓ discrete. Mistakes: of E1–E186, 185 are confirmed (sixteen with a field corrected) and E64 is rejected: Proposition 2.3.19 is openly left as an exercise, and its routine proof is recorded in the review. The review adds E187–E220 (34). Eight of them affect a stated result: E187 (Préface: I′ = ((p−1)/p)I), E193 (Lemme 1.6.8 at ρ = 0), E198 (Théorèmes 2.5.1(2), 3.5.1(2): Spm of the wrong ring), E199 (Proposition 3.1.7: L|F need not be Galois), E211 (Théorème 6.4.4 needs the orbit hypothesis), E215 (Proposition 10.6.18(1) needs k_K algebraically closed), E218 (Proposition 11.2.24 is false: completion is not fully faithful) and E219 (Lemme 11.2.25 is false for non-bijective φ). The lead reviewer re-derived each of these. No erratum or later version exists (Fargues's publications page, the SMF page of Astérisque 406, a web search). The Astérisque text itself was not obtained, so every finding is scoped to the authors' copy.
